worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 65,750.00 + long-term gains 20,000.00 = 85,750.00. Federal taxable income = 85,750.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 70,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 85,750.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 70,000.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 70,000.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 70,000.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 70,000.00; line 2 net long-term gains 20,000.00; line 3 lesser 20,000.00; line 4 ordinary income 70,000.00 - 20,000.00 = 50,000.00; line 5 21,100.00; line 6 21,100.00 - 50,000.00 = -28,900.00, zero or less, so 0.00; line 7 lesser of lines 3 and 6 = 0.00; line 8 3% x 0.00 = 0.00; line 9 20,000.00 - 0.00 = 20,000.00; line 10 4.1% x 20,000.00 = 820.00; line 11 0.00 + 820.00 = 820.00; line 12 ordinary income tax on 50,000.00: 5.9% x 50,000.00 = 2,950.00, less 253 = 2,697.00; line 13 820.00 + 2,697.00 = 3,517.00, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (70,000.00 - 21,100.00 = 48,900.00) = 2,885.10; bracket tax 3,876.80. Gains limited to taxable income: lesser of 20,000.00 and 70,000.00 = 20,000.00; extra rate -1.8% x 20,000.00 = -360.00; 3,876.80 - 360.00 = 3,516.80. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 3,516.80. The form gives 3,517.00; expected keeps the projection's 3,516.80, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). Ordinary income exceeds 21,100, so all the gains pay 4.1%; the only gap is the table constant.
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
